← Week 6

Week 6 · PFA · Tuesday afternoon

Yoga for Body and Mind

Name the poses, sort body and mind benefits, try calm breathing, and design a new pose that could help someone feel better.

Well done!

Start the calm lab

This is a real-life skills activity about using movement and breathing to support your body and your mind. You can do it in order or skip around. Nothing is timed.

Two words for today. Physical means it helps your body, like muscles, balance or flexibility. Mental means it helps your mind, like feeling calmer, focusing, or worrying less.

Student details

What this covers

Pose names, physical and mental benefits, stress coping, exercise and wellbeing, and a creative design challenge.

Round 1: Name the pose

Use the word bank to identify each pose. These are the exact pose images from the worksheet, so the matching should reflect the PDF accurately.

Tree PoseDownward DogChild's PoseWarrior PoseCobra PoseMountain Pose

Older learner link: knowing the name is useful, but recognising the purpose matters too. Tree and Warrior challenge balance and strength; Child's Pose is often used for rest and regulation.

Round 2: Body or mind?

Choose whether each benefit is mostly Physical or Mental. Some benefits can overlap in real life, but these match the worksheet answers.

Round 3: Coping with stress

The worksheet asks about breathing, feel-good brain chemicals, Child's Pose and Cobra Pose. Answer the questions, then try a tiny breathing reset.

Ready

Thirty-second calm reset

Press the button and follow the simple breathing cue. This is not a test. It is just a way to notice your body slowing down.

Round 4: Think about it

Choose a pose for a stressful moment and complete the wellbeing sentence from the worksheet.

Fill the missing words

Doing regular exercise helps our mind because it can clear our _____ and help us to stop _____ about our problems.

Round 5: Design your own pose

Create a new pose. It could help people stretch, balance, or feel happy and relaxed. Draw it, name it, and explain one body benefit and one mind benefit.

Finish and send evidence

The worksheet is finished when you can explain one body benefit, one mind benefit, and one way yoga or exercise could help when someone is stressed.

These are less about memorising answers and more about making safe, sensible choices.

Boss level cleared. Calm, safety and common sense all survived.

Send your work to Jay

The email will include your answers, reflections, and whether you saved a drawing. The drawing itself stays on this device, so Jay may want to see the screen too.
